_comment: Core word sets. Data, not code — read by SceneNavigation.ChromeBundle (what the structure step puts on a home page) AND by the tile picker's filter chips, so the words a caregiver can filter to are the same words the app would add. Every set carries its own `source`: see CoreWordSets.swift for why that field is not optional, and docs/core-vocabulary-audit.md for how these compare to the published lists.

sets.summary: How the child is doing and what they need right now — hungry, thirsty, hurt, happy, sad.

source.label: BlasterAI, in-house
source.detail: Chosen by us. NOT core vocabulary and deliberately not called that: none of these words appears on Universal Core, Banajee (2003), the PRC-Saltillo 100 or CoughDrop's QuickCore 60, because they are states to report rather than words that combine. That is a real and useful thing for a board to carry — it is simply a different thing from core.

sets.summary: High-frequency words that combine and work on any topic — the words AAC research calls core.

source.label: Consensus of four published core lists
source.detail: Every word here appears on at least three of four independently published core-vocabulary lists, and the pronouns on at least two. Taken as an overlap — a fact about where those lists agree — not copied from any one of them. Verified 2026-09-15; see docs/core-vocabulary-audit.md for the full comparison, gaps and licence position.
source.citation: Universal Core, Center for Literacy and Disability Studies, UNC-Chapel Hill (CC BY-SA 4.0) · Banajee, DiCarlo & Buras Stricklin (2003), Augmentative and Alternative Communication 19(2), 67–73 · PRC-Saltillo, 100 Frequently Used Core Words · CoughDrop QuickCore 60
